text:
maria: Heads-up — I pushed a quick prototype dashboard: prompt hitmap + tenant-level savings rollup. Wanted feedback before I wire it into the weekly ops report.

ajay: Nice. Can you drop a link?

maria: https://grafana.internal/r/xyz — it's under "Prompt Cache / Hitmap - Tenant Rollup" (temporary). Shows per-model/per-route heatmap with token-saved estimates aggregated by tenant.

kai: quick glance — heatmap looks useful. How are you computing token-saved? raw hit * avg_response_tokens?

maria: Yeah, naive estimate for now: token_saved = prefix_hit_count * avg_tokens_per_response_for_route. We tag avg_tokens by (model,route) from last 7d.

sasha: Two questions: 1) how do keys map to tenants (are we including anonymized customer ids?), 2) what's the decay window for hits?

maria: 1) We aggregate by tenant_id that is attached to the request metadata before key normalization — we keep it anonymized in dashboards (tenant_###). 2) decay window is 30d by default; heatmap has toggles for 7/30/90d.

oliver: Any change detection? I want to see when per-tenant hit-rate drops suddenly (possible regressed keying).

maria: Added a delta-signal panel: pct_change in hit_rate over last 24h vs prior 24h. Also an alert rule stub (not applied) that triggers if hit_rate drops >20% AND token_saved drops >10k tokens in 1h.

ajay: Alert sounds reasonable. Do we have sampling bias from bots or internal traffic inflating hits?

maria: Good catch. I added an "exclude_sources" filter for known internal apis and health-checks. Also a sample-rate correction factor for high-volume tenants (we upweight downsampled traffic using request sampling metadata).

kai: For keying regressions we should correlate changes in hit-rate with recent deployments and with kernel selection changes. Can we add a small panel that lists recent deploys (deploy-bot) and kernel rollover events?

maria: Sure — can include a timeline band with events pulled from infra events. infra-bot: deploy v3.12.4 to runtime-prod at 1765431000.

sasha: How about warmup signals? We need to show warmup coverage by tenant: fraction of prefixes with warmup-KV present, and average cold penalty (p95 latency delta).

maria: Implemented two warmup panels: (1) percent of requests served with KV-cache hit on first token for tenant, (2) median cold_miss_latency_by_route. Cold penalty computed as p95(latency|miss) - p50(latency|hit).

oliver: Can the dashboard highlight tenants where warmup coverage is below 10% but token-saved potential is high? That would be top candidates for prefetching rules.

maria: Yes — there's an "actionable candidates" table that ranks tenants by estimated monthly token_savings *if warmed* and current coverage. It also suggests warmup batch sizes (based on route avg seq length) and estimated cost to prefetch.

ajay: On instrumentation: are we confident the hit signal is deduplicated across concurrent requests? I saw weird double-counting in staging before.

maria: We introduced edge dedupe using request_id + key hash TTL enforcement in the metric emitter. Metric now has labels: deduped=true/false. Panels use deduped=true.

kai: For perf regressions, can we add a microburst detector — sudden drop in hit-rate for specific (tenant,route) within 5min windows, with automatic sample traces pulled for first 10 occurrences?

maria: Yup, added a microburst alert that captures 10 request traces via trace-batcher and pins them to the incident ticket. It also records kernel selection and batch-size at the time.

sasha: Excellent. One nit — make sure flows that use function-calling or streaming don't pollute avg_tokens estimation. Those are often long-lived and skew mean.

maria: Switched to median tokens and trimmed top/bottom 5% to reduce skew. Also flagged streaming routes separately.

oliver: UX: can we have quick filters for model family (LlamaX, Opti, Redwood-v2) and route tags (chat, embeddings, rerank)?

maria: Done. Filters persist in URL so ops can share links.

ajay: Two follow-ups: 1) Add an export CSV button for top-100 tenants; 2) baseline projection for cost savings if we adopt more aggressive warmup (simulate 50% increment in coverage).

maria: Both on my list. CSV is trivial. Projection runs a monte-carlo using recent variance in avg_tokens per route — will add next.

infra-bot: Note — next infra rollout (kernel optimizer v2) scheduled at 1765438000. Expect brief cache key signature change if deprecated header present.

kai: Flagging: kernel optimizer rollout could change default key normalization; ops to watch hit-rate window after rollout and have rollback plan.

maria: I'll add a post-rollout query that snapshots top-50 tenants' hit-rate and token-saved and diffs against pre-rollout baseline.

ajay: Looks good. Can you assign an owner for the dashboard (oncall?) and a short runbook for what to do on an incident from the alert?

maria: Assigned owner: maria. Runbook stub in the dashboard links to runbook doc: /docs/runbooks/cache-hit-drop.md (still needs expansion).

sasha: LGTM. If we keep panels focused and alerts conservative, this should help us catch real regressions without too much noise. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — I'll iterate based on feedback and drop a note in #eng-runtime when it's promoted to main grafana folder.
